sections.heading: Our Story
sections.body:
Healing Earth Design was founded on the belief that caring for our natural spaces can be a powerful form of healing.

After experiencing personal loss, I returned to school for sustainable horticulture and landscape design, finding peace and purpose through working with plants, soil, and seasonal rhythms. What began as a way to heal grew into a calling to help others reconnect with the earth in meaningful, practical ways.

sections.heading: Who I Am
sections.body:
I'm Sarah Martin, a sustainable horticulture and landscape design graduate with over six years of hands-on gardening experience. My yard serves as a trial garden where I test plants, observe ecosystems, and refine designs before bringing ideas to clients.

I specialize in plant-forward design—no hardscapes, no unnecessary complexity—just thoughtful, site-appropriate plantings that are beautiful, resilient, and supportive of local ecosystems.

sections.heading: My Approach
sections.body:
I believe in "right plant, right place." Every design begins with assessing the space, listening to the client, and what will thrive long-term.

Whether you're a beginner gardener or someone looking to deepen your connection to your outdoor space, I meet you where you are and help you grow with confidence.

sections.heading: Let's Work Together
sections.body:
Healing Earth Design serves homeowners who want gardens that feel alive, intentional, and grounded in sustainability.

If you're ready to create a garden that gives back to you and to the earth, I'd love to work with you.

data.body:
_Last updated October 9, 2026_

This policy explains what Healing Earth Design collects through this website and what happens to it.

## What I collect

When you send the contact form, I receive what you type into it: your name, your email address, the service you're interested in, a preferred date if you give one, your message, and which page you sent it from. Nothing else is collected about you on this site, and there is no advertising or tracking.

## How I use it

A single storefront's plantings are a much smaller change, so we use a fraction of the small-city figure.

faqs.question: Will plantings really bring in more customers?
faqs.answer: No planting guarantees sales. What the research shows is that people say they'd visit more often, stay longer and pay more where a business district is green and cared for. Entrances and patios are where your customers notice it most.

frontmatter.intro: Healing Earth Design is based in Richland, so Kalamazoo County is home ground: consultations, planting plans, installation and seasonal displays for homes and businesses across the county.
frontmatter.growing: Much of Kalamazoo County sits on sandy, well-drained ground, and parts of it, like Gull Prairie around Richland and Prairie Ronde near Schoolcraft, were prairie and oak savanna before they were farmed. That makes it good ground for natives that grew here: little bluestem, butterfly weed, coneflowers, asters and prairie dropseed. Sandy soil dries out by August, so plant choice and mulch matter more than watering.
frontmatter.commercial: From downtown Kalamazoo storefronts and restaurants to offices, medical buildings and apartment communities near the universities, we design and install plantings, run seasonal display programs and care for gardens across the county.

faqs.question: What native plants do well in Kalamazoo County?
faqs.answer: On the county's sandy soils, prairie natives like little bluestem, butterfly weed, purple coneflower, asters and prairie dropseed do well once established. Wetter spots suit swamp milkweed, blue flag iris and sedges.
